Commentary.Commentary: The Kangaroos find spring in their hops - Indeed. The Australians have handed over a morale-deflating loss to the South Africans, and they will have to recover from this rather quickly, as they are placed in what is termed the group of death. Laura Wolvaardt and Co. will now head to Birmingham for their next assignment against Pakistan, and would hope for an improved performance there. As far as Australia are concerned, they take a trip to Leeds, Headingly for their next fixture against Bangladesh Women. Both those games will be played on Wednesday, 17th June. But for now, action shifts to Southampton as the third and final game of this triple-header, Saturday is just about to get underway. West Indies Women take on the defending champions, New Zealand Women, at The Rose Bowl. Our buildup has already begun there, so you can hop to that matchcenter to follow all the updates. From here, it's ta-ta! Goodbye, cheers!

The captain of Australia Women - Sophie Molineux admits that they were in trouble early on, but are really pleased with how the girls responded and how they bowled. She praises the top and middle order for being able to play all around the ground and take the game on, adding that it was great to see the girls play with that freedom. On Litchfield, she calls her amazing, extremely skilful, and says her confidence and game are going through the roof right now. On the bowling changes, she details that she gets a lot of help with that, crediting the team for having the right people in the right places.

The captain of South Africa Women - Laura Wolvaardt admits and says it was a tough day. Reckons that it was a good first half from South Africa, as restricting Australia to that total was a solid effort. However, she admits the batting performance was disappointing. On the total, she feels it was a touch above par, but reckons South Africa would have backed themselves to chase it down, adding they lost momentum heading into the innings. On having Kapp and Ismail back, she says it's awesome to have them in the side, noting it's been a while since South Africa bowled that well in the Powerplay. She also credits Khaka and Mlaba for their work in the middle overs. On her own innings, she admits it was hard to get going and a bit frustrating, with Australia closing off her scoring areas and keeping her quiet. About De Klerk being sent to bat at number four, she says it's nice to stack the lineup that way and have that power coming through the middle order. On bouncing back, she's confident South Africa will, pointing out it's still a long tournament and the plan is to put this game behind them quickly and move forward.
... Time to hear it from the captains ...

It never really got going - South Africa, at the mid innings break, must've been pleased to have restricted Australia below 180, but when they came to chase, it unravelled quickly. They were reduced to 48/3 in 7 overs, but with Laura Wolvaardt and Nadine De Klerk putting on a rebuilding stand of 41, followed by a 34-run alliance between Wolvaardt and Marizanne Kapp, it kept the Proteas in the hunt, well and truly. It wasn't an easy pitch for new batters, with uneven bounce from both ends. The ball kept low from one end, which proved tricky for the Proteas to deal with, and with Australia deploying a full spin attack to choke the flow of runs, that's exactly what happened. The spinners twisted the knife and kept twisting it, accounting for 8 of the 10 wickets, leaving the Proteas with no answers. The fall of Laura Wolvaardt at a crucial time triggered a collapse, and they kept losing wickets one after another, never able to recover.

Breathless first innings - A see-saw innings saw Australia post a competitive 172. They did stutter a bit with the bat, by their standards. Marizanne Kapp struck early with a first-over wicket, and Shabnim Ismail soon removed the dangerous Beth Mooney, leaving Australia in early trouble. Phoebe Litchfield then turned things around with a rapid half-century, anchoring a crucial stand with Ellyse Perry, who started cautiously before accelerating well. South Africa hit back when Nonkululeko Mlaba dismissed Perry in the 16th over, cutting short a promising knock, and another burst of wickets followed before Annabel Sutherland and Nicola Carey provided handy late hits to push the total past 170. South Africa's bowlers shared the load well, with Mlaba the standout, picking up two key wickets while keeping things tight.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - For her outstanding all-round contribution, Georgia Wareham receives the award. She scored a crucial 32 runs with the bat and also picked up 3 massive wickets. On her batting, she says the depth of the lineup lets everyone play with confidence and freedom, knowing what's coming further down the order. She rates Litchfield's knock as awesome today, adding that the group is versatile and it's really just about communicating well within it, something she's enjoyed being part of. On the bowling unit, she notes that she and Ash try to position themselves in the hotspots out in the deep. On Molineux, she says Soph has been brilliant, giving the group plenty of freedom and instilling belief that they're a strong side capable of taking on this tournament, which she calls pretty awesome.

The Aussies boss it up and how​​​​​! As dominant as you like from the six-time World Champions, Australia. They have shown exactly why they remain the yardstick in white-ball cricket and the most successful side in the shortest format of the game. They've also taken brutal revenge for that defeat to the Proteas in the 2024 semifinal, a loss that denied them a seventh title, and set the sails nicely for their journey this time around. A tough, tough outing for the Proteas overall. They have just folded here, losing their last five wickets for just 10 runs. This will massively dent their net run rate moving forward in the tournament. That's a shellacking. Barring three batters, no one from the Proteas unit could cross the double digits. Ouch!

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED AND SIX! That should have been taken as it was a routine chance! Gardner is the guilty party. Flighted up, on off, Nadine De Klerk gets low and looks to sweep it but doesn't get the elevation on it. The ball carries in the deep towards mid-wicket. Ashleigh Gardner settles near the fence only to parry it over the fence. Gardner has taken some of the best chances in the field, so it's a shocking drop from her.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Alana King to Nadine De Klerk, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, on leg, Nadine De Klerk pulls it over mid-wicket for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Alana King to Nadine De Klerk, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Alana King starts with a shorter one, outside off, Nadine De Klerk cuts it to the fielder at backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Alana King to Nadine De Klerk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A good start from the Aussie bowlers. They have got the Proteas under pressure and desperate for a rebuild. Alana King is now introduced into the attack.

FOUR! Streaky boundary for Laura Wolvaardt but she wouldn't mind the way it comes as long as it comes. On a length, around off, shaping away from the batter. Laura Wolvaardt looks to flick across the line but gets lucky to get an outside edge that flies behind square on the off side towards the third man region for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Kim Garth to Laura Wolvaardt, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched-up delivery, around off, Laura Wolvaardt gets right on top of the bounce, meets the ball underneath her eyeline and drills this well but finds the figure of Kim Garth in her followthrough.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Kim Garth to Laura Wolvaardt, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and wide outside off, Nadine De Klerk slaps this towards the right of sweeper cover for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Kim Garth to Nadine De Klerk, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, around off, Nadine De Klerk punches this to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Kim Garth to Nadine De Klerk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and down the leg side, Nadine De Klerk goes for a paddle sweep but misses. This was not that wide, even being down the leg side and the umpire kept her arms down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Kim Garth to Nadine De Klerk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Laura's off-side game is a treat to watch for all. Back of a length, around off, Laura Wolvaardt gets up on her toes and punches this off her back foot towards sweeper cover for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Kim Garth to Laura Wolvaardt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through around off, Nadine De Klerk pushes this to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Sophie Molineux to Nadine De Klerk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This has travelled the distance. Flighted, around off, Nadine De Klerk takes a long stride out in front, sweeps this aerially with an intention to clear the fence and she does that with ease. The fielder at deep square leg was ball-watching as this one cleared the fence to her left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Sophie Molineux to Nadine De Klerk, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated into the batter, on middle and leg, Nadine De Klerk tucks this to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Sophie Molineux to Nadine De Klerk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nerves are telling on the Proteas batters. Arm-delivery, around middle and leg, Nadine De Klerk shimmies down the track and goes for a wild slog. Gets an inside edge that strikes back onto her pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Sophie Molineux to Nadine De Klerk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker one, around off, Nadine De Klerk blocks this off her front foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Sophie Molineux to Nadine De Klerk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted around the pads, Laura Wolvaardt rolls her wrists and flicks this to long on for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Sophie Molineux to Laura Wolvaardt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kim goes full again, bowls it around off, Nadine De Klerk drives this to sweeper cover for a couple. A slight misfield by Megan Schutt at sweeper cover and this could have been four, but she recovers well and flicks this ball back inside the playing area just in time. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Kim Garth to Nadine De Klerk, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Like Australia, it's been a sloppy start for the Proteas in their run hunt. Oh, a promotion for Nadine De Klerk as she comes in at number 4.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! Kim Garth comes back in the best possible way by dismissing Annerie Dercksen. Kim drags her length back, bowls it on a good length and keeps it in the line of the stumps. Annerie Dercksen gets beaten to the pace as she brings her bat down and the ball hits her front pad and deflects onto the top of off, rattling the timber.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Kim Garth to Annerie Dercksen, OUT! b Kim Garth.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! This is a classy shot from Annerie Dercksen. Slightly pitched-up delivery, around off, Annerie Dercksen steps down the track and offers a full face of her bat to loft this over the bowler for a boundary down in front of the sight screen.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Kim Garth to Annerie Dercksen, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Mel Jones informs on air that Phoebe Litchfield is off the field for now. Not quite sure who the sub fielder is in for her. Nasser Hussain reckons it could be down to the blow Litchfield took on her shoulder while batting in the first innings.
Good length, and around leg, Annerie Dercksen tucks this to mid-wicket for a dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Kim Garth to Annerie Dercksen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, around off, Annerie Dercksen gets up on her toes and pats this back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Kim Garth to Annerie Dercksen, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, around off, Laura Wolvaardt strides close to the pitch of the ball and drives this through the covers region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Kim Garth to Laura Wolvaardt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: What a start from Sophie Molineux. A wicket and just two runs off the first over. Annerie Dercksen walks in to bat now. Kim Garth will share the attack from the other end for South Africa Women.

OUT! LBW! Sophie strikes in the very first over and South Africa Women are at 2 for 1. Sophie uses the width of the crease, goes a tad wide as she bowls it with a slightly round-arm action. Keeps the ball in line with the sticks and bowls this around that nagging length. Sune Luus rocks back and swipes across the line but misses and gets hit on her back pad. A loud appeal and the umpire acknowledges it by raising her finger. Luus walks back without reviewing.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Sophie Molineux to Sune Luus, OUT! lbw b Sophie Molineux.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker and flatter, down the leg side. Laura Wolvaardt comes inside the ine of the ball and helps this towards the right of the short fine leg fielder for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Sophie Molineux to Laura Wolvaardt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, on middle and leg, Sune Luus goes deep inside her crease and milks this through mid-wicket for a single to set the chase kicking.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Sophie Molineux to Sune Luus, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated full and on middle and off, Sune keeps her calm and pushes this back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Sophie Molineux to Sune Luus, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Arm-delivery, around off, Luus rocks back and cuts this well but straight to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Sophie Molineux to Sune Luus, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sophie starts with a slower one, tossed up around the pads. Sune Luus pushes this back tot he bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Sophie Molineux to Sune Luus, No run.
